prerequisites: General knowledge of technical activities in the field of data science and engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with theoretical and practical knowledge to organize, plan, and manage a project, based on their existing technical knowledge.
Enable students to prepare documents associated with a project, analyze its viability, and carry out its processing, including the contracting phase.
Know the most used standards for project management and be able to apply them in the context of data science and engineering.
Identify project risks and develop plans for their management.
Enable students to work in multidisciplinary environments and lead work teams in projects.
Enable students to plan and direct innovation projects.
Knowledge of project types, methodologies, and standards.
Be able to document, plan, and budget projects.
Manage human resources of a project.
Contract and bid for projects in compliance with regulations.
Know and apply key aspects in project costs, deadlines, and quality.

syllabus_topics: The project: concept, types, and characteristics.
Methodologies and standards for project management in predictive and adaptive environments.
Preliminary studies and project viability analysis.
Budgeting and management of project costs and risks.
Group project from conception to preparation of documentation for contracting and other associated documentation.
Individual practices with planning tools (Microsoft Project).

assessment_methods.method: Group work (memory, reports, oral presentation and defense)
Continuous evaluation: Attendance and participation in Seminars and Tutorials
Continuous evaluation: Active participation in forums and virtual campus activities
Final in-person knowledge test (test, short questions, application cases, problem solving)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a score equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 must be obtained in both the final in-person test and the practical part of the course. Activities not completed or not submitted will be counted as zero. If the minimum score is not reached in any of the tests, the final numerical grade will be the minimum grade of the tests. In the extraordinary call, approved work from the ordinary call will be taken into account, or replaced by an equivalent individual assignment. A new in-person knowledge test will be conducted. The final grade for the extraordinary call is calculated as: Final Grade = 0.65 x In-person test + 0.35 x Work Grade, requiring at least 5 in each part. For differentiated evaluation, students are exempt from mandatory attendance to practices. Their mastery of course concepts will be assessed through an exam (65% of the final grade) and an individual substitute work (35% of the final grade), requiring at least 5 in each part.
